title: Father's sticks and perforated duplex snare drum
summary: Light number-five sticks, snare on the street, and the nickel and brass perforated duplex snares, one now owned by Lester.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Do you remember, did he ever say, or do you remember personally, what kind of sticks he used if they were heavy or lightweight or longer than usual or what kind of? They were just about number five, I think, in those times.
They were running by numbers. They weren't real heavy sticks.
They weren't real heavy sticks.
No, he never used real heavy sticks.
He used heavier ones on the street by any chance. No, the same sticks. He would use the same sticks each time. And on the street did he usually play the snare drum? Most of the time. I know.
Most of the time he used snare drum.
Did he use the same snare drum that he used in a dance orchestra?

Well, he did, but he had on the last, he was using a duplex out on the street. It was a duplex snare drum. I think Lester San Diego had one of the models of the one that he had. I think Lester has it now.
Can I believe Alfred Williams, doesn't that, a duplex? The one that boy from England here last year bought one from Alfred Williams. Yeah, I'm not sure. I think it was. I believe it is a duplex.

Because at the time it was only two in town. It was one that was of nickel and one of brass. And my father had both of them. The first one he had bought was the one with brass. And then he gave or traded that one over to a drummer during that period by the name of Wooligan. Now, I think his name was William Wooligan or Bill Wooligan. And he had the nickel one. And that was the only two that I've ever seen. And I do believe the one that San Diego had now is the one that my father had. Is he really? I believe that's the one.
When you say of nickel and of brass, you mean the rods on it or?
No, the shell.
Well, it wasn't a wooden shell.
Where the head was was wooden, but the shell was nickel. It was nickel and it was a brass shell and it was perforated.
Then the rim around up at the top was wood.
Was wood. That's correct. That's correct.
You say it's perforated?
Yeah, it was perforated. The shell was.
With holes in it?
Yeah, holes in it. Very light. Maybe, I mean, it really was a light drum. It's nothing like with the drum now because the snare drum now hit much heavier than what that was. Yeah.

Was it a very deep one, you know, say five or six things or seven or eight or? Just about five or six. Five or six rather. Just about. Shallower, medium. Just about what they use practically now. And he didn't use a deeper drum on the street?
No, no. Never did. It was just.
